corrected_verdict.rationale: Handoff omits required elements; receiver cannot act without re-contacting customer.

description: Phi-4-mini consistently accepted incomplete handoffs by inferring missing elements rather than verifying they were present. Across all 13 disagreements (gold=FAIL, Qwen=FAIL, Phi=PASS), Phi invented justifications like 'implied customer contacted customer service first', 'not specified but implied', 'urgency implied by customer dissatisfaction' to fill in elements the handoff did not actually contain.
what_judge_should_learn: Handoff completeness requires each required element to be explicitly stated, not inferred from context. A judge that credits implied or inferrable elements will let thin handoffs pass. The rubric must distinguish 'element is present' from 'element could be inferred by a reader'.
notes: Qwen had 0 failures on detailed_with_examples — this pattern is a Phi failure mode, not a Qwen failure mode. Relevant for any future Phi fine-tuning or for strengthening rubric language to block inference-based scoring.

corrected_verdict.rationale: Vague rubric caused Qwen to invent requirements not in the gold standard, flagging valid handoffs as incomplete.

description: Vague rubric produced 35% false-unsafe rate (7/20 pass examples flagged as fail). Without a concrete checklist of required elements, Qwen applied stricter standards than gold labels — flagging handoffs that were genuinely complete but lacked elements the vague rubric left undefined. The false-unsafe problem is the inverse of the false-safe problem: a rubric that is too open-ended causes over-flagging of good responses.
what_judge_should_learn: For checklist-type failure modes (handoff completeness, SOP adherence), vague rubrics produce false-unsafe errors because the judge invents requirements not in the gold standard. The fix is always explicit enumeration of required elements — not softer language. This is the same lesson as Judge 2 (SOP adherence).
notes: Confirms the pattern: holistic judges (source_of_truth, unsupported_promise) tolerate vague rubrics; checklist judges (sop_adherence, handoff_completeness) require explicit element lists.
